title: KASA Hosts 5th Aerospace SOS Consultative Meeting on Space Transportation (Hanwha, KAI, 9 others)
text: KASA Hosts 5th Aerospace SOS Consultative Meeting on Space Transportation. Date 2026-05-15. Discussions on Revitalizing the Nuri Industry Ecosystem and Developing a Private-Sector-Led Space Transportation Sector. Emphasizing Stable Launch Opportunities and Public-Private Collaboration. The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) held the 5th Aerospace SOS Consultation Meeting on Thursday, May 14, at Hanwha Aerospace's 1st Plant in Seongsan-gu, Changwon, Gyeongsangnam-do. The meeting brought together representatives from the industry to explore ways to revitalize the Nuri rocket (KSLV-II) launch ecosystem and promote private-sector-led growth in the space transportation sector. Participating companies (11): Hanwha Aerospace, Korean Aerospace Industry (KAI), Doowon Heavy Industries, Vitzro Nextech, SPACEPRO, S&K Aerospace, Uconsystem, HyLok Corporation, Danam Systems, HIZE Composite Industries and HANYANG ENG. Hanwha Aerospace, the system integrator, shared the status of preparations for the Nuri's 5th launch and upcoming missions. Currently, the assembly of the Nuri 5 vehicle is 70-90% complete, with a targeted launch in the third quarter of 2026. This mission is planned to deploy five microsatellite constellations and ten secondary payload satellites into sun-synchronous orbit. Administrator Taeseog Oh quoted.

title: KASA Develops Satellite Imagery AI Training Data Tailored to Industry Needs (KASA+KARI+SPAID+Seoul Nat'l Univ Sci&Tech)
text: KASA Develops Satellite Imagery AI Training Data Tailored to Industry Needs. Date 2026-05-15. Satellite Imagery AI Datasets Incorporating Industry Feedback to be Released this Year. The Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA, Administrator Taeseog Oh) announced that it will host the Industry Roundtable on Utilization of Satellite Imagery Big Data and AI Training Data on Friday, May 15, at the Daejeon Convention Center (DCC). The event aims to identify industry demand for satellite imagery AI training data and explore necessary policy support measures for domestic companies specializing in satellite imagery and artificial intelligence (AI). KASA and the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) will share the current status of publicly available satellite imagery AI training data. In 2023 and 2024, a total of 630,000 datasets were released, covering key satellite imagery applications such as object detection, building segmentation, road extraction, cloud detection, and land cover classification. More recently, in 2025 and early this year, an additional 300,000 datasets were released, expanding the applications to include ocean and glacier monitoring, as well as time-series land cover change detection. SPAID Inc. has applied these datasets to develop 3D geospatial AI solutions. Research teams at Seoul National University of Science and Technology have incorporated the datasets. Kyungwon Rho, Vice Administrator of KASA, quoted: 'we will actively promote open access to data from the Korea Multi-Purpose Satellites (KOMPSATs) and the next-generation mid-sized satellites (CAS500s)'.
